services.heading: AI chatbots and assistants for agencies
services.seo_description: White-label AI chatbot builds for agencies: assistants that answer from your client's own content, cite sources and hand off to a person. See how we scope.
services.intro: We build white-label AI chatbots and assistants that your agency sells as its own. Each one answers from the client's approved content, shows where the answer came from and passes the visitor to a person when it should.
services.content_html:
A white-label AI chatbot is an on-site or messaging assistant that we build and your agency delivers under its own brand. The client sees your agency's work, and we never contact them.

What a white-label AI chatbot should and should not do

It should answer from the client's own content and admit when it cannot. It should not guess a price, a policy or a delivery date.

We build it on retrieval. The client's pages, product data, policies and help articles are indexed, and each answer is drawn from those sources with a link back.

Tone rules keep it in the client's voice. Refusal rules cover what it must not answer, such as legal or medical advice, or a price the content does not state.

Edge cases matter more than the demo. Visitors try to make it say odd things, pages contradict each other, content goes out of date and people paste personal details into the chat. We test for each before launch and set a schedule for refreshing the index.

Our plugin or a custom build

For many WordPress clients our own plugin is the quicker route. A custom build fits when knowledge lives in several systems, the site is not WordPress, or the agent must carry only your brand today.

SituationBest fitWhy
A WordPress site selling services or WooCommerce productsThe free SoftVolt AI Voice Agent pluginVoice and text chat, bookings, hand-offs and a leads inbox already exist. Speech runs in the visitor's browser, so voice adds no cost.
The agent must show only your agency's or the client's brand nowA custom buildWhite label and agency mode are planned for the plugin's Pro add-on, which is not available yet.
Knowledge sits in PDFs, a help desk or several systemsA custom assistant on the Claude or OpenAI API with vector searchRetrieval works across every source, with citations, inside a widget built in Next.js.
The client already uses a live chat toolAn integration into that toolTheir team keeps one inbox, and the assistant hands over inside it.

Measuring whether it works

Every assistant ships with an evaluation set: real visitor queries with the answers the client signed off. We re-run it whenever the content, prompt or model changes.

The monthly review shows what the assistant answered, what it refused and what it passed to a person. Unanswered queries become content tasks, which gives your team a list of pages worth writing.

We do not promise a deflection rate before launch. We agree what to measure at scoping and report it plainly.

Pricing, data and the wider picture

A custom assistant gets a written scope and a fixed price within two business days of the brief. Model usage is billed at cost or runs on an API account in your name or your client's. See the current plans on our rates page.

Chat transcripts can hold personal data, so we name the model provider in the data processing agreement. For UK and EU visitors we work under the UK IDTA or EU Standard Contractual Clauses, as our security page sets out.

Assistants often sit inside a wider process, such as routing leads to a CRM. That work is covered by our white-label AI automation and workflow automation services.

Questions agencies ask about white-label AI chatbots

Will the chatbot make things up?

It is built not to. It answers only from the client's approved content, shows the source and refuses when the content does not cover the topic.

No model is perfect, so we re-run the evaluation set on every change and review real conversations each month. Anything sensitive, such as a complaint or a refund request, goes to a person.

Can the chatbot carry only our agency's or the client's brand?

With a custom build, yes. The widget, the name and the voice belong to the client, and nothing mentions us.

Our free plugin does not offer white label mode yet, as that is planned for its Pro add-on. For an unbranded agent today, we scope a custom assistant under your brand.

Which AI model runs it, and who pays?

Custom assistants run on the Claude API or the OpenAI API, chosen from the evaluation results for that client's content. Usage is billed at cost or held in your or your client's account, with no mark-up. Our plugin also works with free tiers from OpenRouter, Groq and Gemini, which suits a trial.

Where are the conversations stored?

In a database the client owns. With our plugin that is their own WordPress database, where only administrators can see leads.

Custom builds use a PostgreSQL database in the client's hosting account. For UK and EU visitors we work under a data processing agreement, with the model provider named as a sub-processor.

Can it book appointments or take payments?

Our plugin books services and saves each booking in WordPress, and in a WooCommerce shop it adds products to the cart for the normal checkout. Payments in the chat are planned for Pro, not available today. A custom assistant can connect to the client's booking system where that system has an API, which we confirm at scoping.

services.heading: White-label AI automation for agencies
services.seo_description: White-label AI automation for agencies: lead handling, reporting and support triage on Claude and OpenAI APIs, under your brand. Get a fixed-price scope.
services.intro: SoftVolt AI is a white-label AI automation team for agencies in the UK, US, Canada and Australia. We build lead handling, reporting and support workflows on the Claude and OpenAI APIs, under your brand. You get a written scope and fixed price within two business days of the brief.
services.content_html:
White-label AI automation lets your agency sell AI work to clients without hiring an AI developer. You bring the client and the problem. We scope and build the automation on the Claude or OpenAI API, then hand it back with your name on every document.

Every automation starts as one measurable task, and a person approves anything that reaches a customer.

What is white-label AI automation?

White-label AI automation is AI workflow development that an outside team builds and your agency delivers as its own. The partner connects a model such as Claude or GPT to the client's forms, inbox or CRM, and adds the checks a business needs. The partner stays invisible: no credit, no client contact.

In practice, one defined job moves from a person to software, such as sorting overnight enquiries or drafting the monthly report from live figures. Agencies use it to add AI to their offer without carrying the cost of a specialist hire.

AI automation for agencies: what we handle and what you keep

We handle the design, build and testing of the automation. You keep the client, the decision about what the AI is allowed to do, and the price you charge for it.

Many briefs start vague: the client wants "some AI" and nobody has defined the job. Our first job is finding the task that eats the most hours and is safe to automate, then timing it as it runs today.

Tasks that suit AI automation

  • Lead qualification: read each enquiry, score it against the client's criteria, route it to the right person and draft a reply for approval.
  • Report drafting: pull the month's figures from the ad platforms and analytics, then draft commentary your account manager edits.
  • Support triage: tag and prioritise incoming tickets, and suggest replies from the client's help content.
  • Content pipelines: product descriptions drafted from a spreadsheet, with an editor's sign-off before publishing.

The edge cases we plan for

Language models give slightly different answers to the same input. So we keep an evaluation set: real examples with the answer you expect, re-run whenever a prompt or model changes.

Providers also retire models and change their limits. We pin model versions where the API allows and queue requests, so an outage delays work instead of losing it.

Every run is logged with its token use, and you get a monthly usage report to check against the cost model agreed at scoping. A kill switch lets your team pause the automation without calling a developer.

Which approach fits which client

The right approach depends on whether the task needs judgement or only rules. Match the client's problem to the build below, and treat AI as one step inside a workflow rather than the whole product.

Client needApproachWhy
Leads land in three inboxes and a spreadsheetWorkflow automation in n8n, Make or codeMoving and deduplicating data is a rules job. A model would add cost and risk for no gain.
Enquiries need reading, sorting and a first replyAn AI step inside a workflow, with approval before anything is sentModels read messy text well. A person still checks what goes out under the client's name.
Website visitors ask the same things all dayAn AI assistant grounded in the client's contentAnswers come from approved pages with a source, and the visitor reaches a person when the assistant cannot help.
A WordPress site needs a voice or chat agent that books servicesOur SoftVolt AI Voice Agent pluginIt already handles bookings, hand-offs and lead alerts, so setup can replace a custom build when the brief fits.
The client's team runs the business on a spreadsheetAn internal tool on Next.js and PostgreSQLIt gives the team roles, an audit trail and validated imports, which a shared sheet cannot.

Where AI automation is a poor fit

We will tell you when AI is the wrong tool. If the rule can be written down, plain code is cheaper and never improvises.

We also steer clients away from AI for exact calculations, and for advice a customer will act on with no human check. A task done twice a month rarely repays the build cost either.

How a project runs with your agency

Every project runs through one named producer in a shared Slack Connect or WhatsApp channel, from brief to handover. You get a written scope and a fixed price within two business days, and nothing starts until you approve it.

Our team is in Dhaka (UTC+6, no daylight saving). Our afternoon overlaps the UK working day, our evening covers US East Coast mornings, and our morning meets the Sydney afternoon. Brief us at 5pm London and review at 9am.

Automations run against test data and past examples before they touch a live account. Staging, commit messages and documents carry your agency's name. The evaluation results come with the handover, so you can show the client what was tested.

Pricing for AI automation work

AI automation is part of our Premium plan, from £2,400 a month, and of the Enterprise plan, which is quoted. Premium covers up to 6 active projects at a time, a named producer and shared channel, and priority support with a same-day response.

A one-off automation outside a plan gets its own written scope and fixed price. These things move that price most:

  • How many systems the automation connects to, and how clean their data is
  • Whether the output reaches customers, which adds an approval flow and more testing
  • The size of the evaluation set the task needs before it can go live
  • Where it runs: n8n cloud, a self-hosted n8n instance or a custom Node.js service

AI usage, n8n and other tool costs are billed at cost or held in your own accounts, with no mark-up. Every plan and its inclusions are on our rates page.

Builds you can open

None of the eight case studies on this site is an AI automation project, and we will not present one as if it were. Two things are open for you to check instead.

The first is our own SoftVolt AI Voice Agent WordPress plugin. It answers visitors by voice or text, using only the facts it is given, and hands hot leads to a person.

It is free on WordPress.org. Install it on a test site and check how it keeps API keys server-side and caps daily messages.

The second is The Bulk Bag Man headless build, delivered by our founder. Contact form submissions pass through a Next.js route handler, so the browser never talks to WordPress directly. Our AI integrations follow the same rule: API keys stay on the server.

In-house hire, freelancer or white-label partner

A white-label partner suits agencies that sell AI work regularly but cannot keep a specialist busy every week. An in-house hire makes sense once automation is a steady, full-time workload.

Who manages the workYou doYou doA named producer in your shared channel
Range of skillsWhatever one hire knowsUsually one specialismAI automation plus the WordPress or Next.js site it plugs into
TestingOne person checking their own workDepends on the individualAn evaluation set agreed at scoping and re-run on every change
When it endsNotice periods and a new searchA scramble to recover files and loginsHandover with documentation, and our access revoked

Your client stays yours

We will not approach, quote for or accept work from your client, during the project or after it. There are no footer links or "built by" lines, and no portfolio use without your written permission.

Credentials live in a shared 1Password or Bitwarden vault, never in email. We take the least access the work needs, such as a scoped WordPress role rather than an owner login. We revoke it at handover and confirm that in writing.

Client data and AI APIs

AI automation often sends client data to a model provider, so we name that provider as a sub-processor in the data processing agreement. Bangladesh is not on the EU adequacy list, so UK and EU personal data moves under the UK IDTA or Addendum and EU SCCs.

We design each automation to send only the fields the task needs. The API account can sit in your name or your client's, so the data relationship stays with them. Read every practice on our security and confidentiality page.

Working with agencies in the UK, US, Canada and Australia

For UK agencies

Our afternoon in Dhaka runs alongside your working day, so a brief sent at 5pm London can be in review by 9am. We handle client personal data under UK GDPR, with the IDTA or UK Addendum and an Article 28 agreement.

For US, Canadian and Australian agencies

Our evening overlaps Eastern Time mornings in New York and Toronto, and our morning overlaps the Sydney afternoon. If a client has sector rules on data, such as in health or finance, say so in the brief and we will scope around them.

Questions agencies ask about white-label AI automation

Will our client know you built the automation?

Not from us. Staging, commit messages, documentation and reports carry your agency's brand, and we never contact your client.

If the automation sends emails or messages, they go out from the client's own accounts and addresses. Our name does not appear in workflow names, code comments or the handover pack.

Can we run a white-label AI agency offer without hiring?

Yes. You sell and scope the work with your client and keep the relationship. We design, build and document each automation under your brand.

AI automation sits in our Premium and Enterprise plans, and one-off projects get a fixed price, so you can start with a single automation.

Do you build n8n automation for agencies, or only custom code?

Both. We use n8n or Make when a visual workflow fits, because your team can read it and change small things later.

We write custom Node.js code when volumes are high, the logic is complex or the data needs strict validation. Self-hosted n8n keeps data on your own infrastructure.

Can we resell a white-label AI voice agent to clients?

Partly, today. Our SoftVolt AI Voice Agent plugin is free on WordPress.org, and you can install it on client sites now.

White label and agency mode are planned for its Pro add-on, which is still being built. If a client needs a fully unbranded voice or chat agent now, we scope a custom build under your brand instead.

Which AI models do you use, and who pays for them?

We build on the Claude API and the OpenAI API, and pick the model for each task from its evaluation results. Usage is billed at cost or runs on an API account in your name or your client's, with no mark-up. The monthly usage report shows what each automation costs to run.

How do you stop the AI sending something wrong?

With guardrails agreed at scoping. Anything that reaches a customer passes an approval step, and you decide if and when that step is relaxed.

Prompts tell the model to refuse rather than guess when the source data is missing. Every run is logged, and a kill switch lets your team pause the automation without a developer.

Is it safe to send client data to an AI API?

It can be, with the right paperwork and design. We name the model provider as a sub-processor in the data processing agreement.

UK or EU personal data moves under the IDTA, UK Addendum or Standard Contractual Clauses. We send only the fields a task needs, and keep credentials in a shared vault with access revoked at handover.

What happens if an automation breaks after launch?

If the failure sits inside the agreed scope, we fix it at our cost. Logging and alerts make a failed run visible rather than silent, and queued requests wait out a provider outage. Changes on the provider's side, such as a retired model, are handled under your monthly plan or quoted as a small fixed-price change.

What do you need from us to quote?

A plain description of the task, a handful of real examples with the result you expect, rough monthly volumes and the systems involved. Redacted examples are fine before the NDA is signed. We reply within one business day and send a written scope with a fixed price within two business days of the brief.

services.heading: GA4, GTM and conversion tracking setup
services.seo_description: White-label GA4 and conversion tracking for agencies: Tag Manager, Google Ads and Meta conversions and Consent Mode v2, documented. See what we test.
services.intro: White-label GA4 and conversion tracking for agencies that need numbers a client can trust. We plan the events, build the Tag Manager container, connect Google Ads and Meta, and test every consent state. You present the setup and the dashboard as your own work.
services.content_html:
White-label GA4 and conversion tracking means we build and verify a client's measurement, and your agency delivers it under its own name. We work inside the client's GA4 property and Tag Manager container with scoped access, and document every tag so your team can explain the setup in a meeting.

Most broken tracking fails quietly. A tag fires twice, a form event fires on page load, or a consent banner blocks everything and nobody notices for a month. Our job is to find those faults before your client does.

What goes into white-label GA4 and conversion tracking

It starts with a measurement plan, not with tags. We agree which actions count as leads or sales, then name events consistently so reports still make sense a year later.

  • GA4 key events that match the client's real goals, with smaller actions kept as ordinary events so they do not inflate results.
  • A Tag Manager container you can read: clear tag names, folders by platform, notes on every trigger and version notes that say what changed.
  • Google Ads conversions with the right counting method, so one enquiry counts once and each purchase counts every time.
  • Meta Pixel and Conversions API sending matching event IDs, so Meta can remove duplicates.
  • E-commerce events on WooCommerce or Shopify, checked against real orders in the store admin.

Consent Mode v2 setup that keeps the data usable

Consent Mode v2 tells Google tags what each visitor agreed to, so tags adjust instead of breaking. Google requires it for visitors in the UK and EEA if the client wants to keep building remarketing audiences in Google Ads.

We set consent defaults before any tag loads, wire the banner to update all four consent signals, and test each state: accept all, reject all and partial choices. Rejecting must be as easy as accepting. We use the client's existing banner if it is sound, or set up c15t if it is not.

We agree basic or advanced mode with you. Basic mode loads Google tags only after consent, while advanced mode sends cookieless pings so Google can model the gaps. In both cases, no tracking cookie is set before the visitor chooses.

Where the client's data and budget justify it, we also scope server-side options such as the Meta Conversions API.

When the ad platform and the CRM disagree

They will never match exactly, but every gap should have a reason you can explain. We trace a sample of real leads from click to CRM and write down where each difference comes from.

Common causes include different attribution windows, view-through conversions, duplicate form events, thank-you pages that count reloads, and visitors who rejected cookies. Once the causes are written down, your account manager can answer the client's hard question with facts.

Pushing form leads into the CRM with source data attached sits in our workflow automation service.

Access, pricing and where this fits

We never need owner logins. Credentials stay in a shared vault and access is revoked at handover, as our security and confidentiality page sets out.

A tracking setup or audit gets a written scope and fixed price within two business days of the brief. Ongoing measurement can sit inside a monthly plan, and the rates page shows what each plan includes.

Tracking supports our white-label digital marketing work and our conversion rate optimisation, because neither works on broken numbers. PPC teams can see how we work with Google Ads and PPC agencies.

Questions agencies ask about GA4 and conversion tracking

Can you fix a GA4 setup someone else built?

Yes. We audit the GA4 property and the Tag Manager container first, list what each tag does, and flag anything firing twice, firing early or not firing at all.

You get the audit as a document in your brand, then a fixed-price scope for the fixes. Nothing changes in the container until you approve it.

Does Consent Mode v2 reduce the conversions we report?

Usually yes, because visitors who reject cookies are no longer tracked in the normal way. Advanced mode lets Google model some of those conversions, which narrows the gap. We show the client the before and after with that explanation attached, so a lower number reads as accurate measurement rather than a campaign problem.

Do you offer server-side tracking?

Where it earns its cost. The Meta Conversions API is the common example, and a server-side Tag Manager container is an option for larger accounts.

Server-side setups need hosting, which the client pays for at cost with no mark-up. We explain the trade-offs first and scope it separately, so nobody signs up for running costs they did not expect.

Will the Looker Studio dashboard carry our branding?

Yes. Dashboards use your logo, colours and report structure, and our name appears nowhere. We build them on data sources the client or your agency owns, so the dashboard keeps working after handover and you can edit it without us.

What do you need from us to start?

Access to the GA4 property, Tag Manager, the ad accounts and the website, shared through a password vault. A short note on what counts as a lead or sale for this client, and which CRM receives them. If you already have a measurement plan or a client complaint about the numbers, send that too.

services.heading: White-label CRO for agencies
services.seo_description: White-label conversion rate optimisation for agencies: funnel diagnosis, faster landing pages and A/B tests, delivered under your brand. See how it runs.
services.intro: White-label conversion rate optimisation for agencies whose clients already pay for traffic. We find where visitors drop out, fix the pages and forms, and test changes where volume allows. It all runs under your brand, with a fixed price agreed first.
services.content_html:
White-label conversion rate optimisation means we find and build the changes that turn more of a client's traffic into leads or orders. Your agency presents the work as its own, and you keep the strategy and the client conversation.

The same team writes the code and reads the data, so a recommendation does not sit in a queue waiting for a developer. That matters on paid campaigns, where a weak page wastes budget every day.

What white-label conversion rate optimisation covers

It covers everything from the ad click to the lead in the CRM, starting with the numbers.

  • Tracking before opinions. We confirm that GA4 and the ad platforms record conversions correctly. A broken form event can make a good page look like a failure.
  • Message match. We compare what each ad group promises with the headline and offer on its landing page.
  • Friction in forms and checkout. Extra fields, unclear error messages, slow payment steps and booking widgets that break on small screens.
  • Speed. Slow or jumpy pages lose visitors early, so we fix load time too, using our Core Web Vitals and speed work.
  • Behaviour data. Heatmaps and session recordings in Microsoft Clarity, loaded only after consent, with form inputs masked.

You stay in charge of the offer, pricing and anything that needs the client's sign-off. We bring evidence; you decide what goes to the client.

A/B testing or direct fixes: which fits the page

Run a split test when the page has enough conversions to give a clear answer in a few weeks. When it does not, ship the fix and measure before and after.

Plenty of lead-generation pages get a handful of enquiries a week, and a test on that volume can run for months without a result. For those pages we make the change, note the release date and compare results with the same tracking.

Since Google Optimize closed, tests run through other tools or variants built into the page code. On Next.js we can serve variants from the server, so visitors never see the original page flash first.

How a CRO engagement runs with your agency

Each round starts with a written list of fixes, ranked by likely impact and effort, which you can forward to the client as your own.

You approve the list. We build the changes on a staging URL under your brand and release them when you say so. A named producer runs the shared channel, so your account manager always knows who to ask.

Each month you get a short report in your template: what changed, when it went live and what the numbers did next. It says which changes were tested and which were judgement calls. We never promise a conversion uplift, because traffic quality and the offer move the result too.

The team works from Dhaka (UTC+6), so a brief sent at 5pm London can be ready for review at 9am.

Pricing and builds you can open

A one-off CRO audit and fix sprint gets a written scope and a fixed price within two business days of the brief. Ongoing work runs on a monthly plan, and Premium (from £2,400/month) is the tier that covers builds, SEO and paid media together. The rates page lists every plan.

For a build you can click through, open the Patriot Insurance Group case study. Our founder built its enquiry and quote-request flows as full-stack developer before SoftVolt AI.

CRO is part of our white-label digital marketing service and pairs with white-label Google Ads management.

Questions agencies ask about white-label CRO

Will our client know we use a CRO partner?

Not from us. Staging URLs, reports and documents carry your agency's brand, and we sign a mutual NDA before you share client details.

We never contact your client, by email, LinkedIn or anything else. If the client wants to meet the person doing the work, that is your call to make.

What access do you need to ad accounts and GA4?

The lowest level that does the job: GA4 property access, a Tag Manager user role, read access to the ad accounts and an editor role on the site.

Credentials live in a shared password vault, never in email. We revoke access at handover and confirm it in writing.

How much traffic does a page need for A/B testing?

It depends on conversions, not visits. Before proposing a test, we estimate how long it would need to run at the page's current conversion volume.

If the answer is several months, we recommend direct fixes measured before and after instead. That way your client never pays for a test that cannot reach a clear result.

Can you improve landing pages another developer built?

Yes. CRO work usually starts on pages someone else built, on WordPress, Elementor or Next.js. We review the build first, so we know which changes are quick and which fight the theme.

If a page cannot reach acceptable speed, we quote a rebuild as a high-speed landing page, as a separate fixed-price option.

Do you guarantee a higher conversion rate?

No. Conversion rate depends on traffic quality, the offer, pricing and the season as well as the page, and nobody controls all of those.

What we commit to is a documented process: tracked changes, honest reporting of what worked and what did not, and a clear plan for the next round.

services.heading: White-label Elementor development for agencies
services.seo_description: White-label Elementor development for agencies: custom widgets, theme builder templates, global styles and speed fixes under your brand, at a fixed price.
services.intro: Our white-label Elementor development gives your clients page-builder editing with the design kept in check: custom widgets, theme builder templates and a global style system, delivered under your brand. Your client edits the content they should, with far fewer ways to break the layout.
services.content_html:
What white-label Elementor development covers

White-label Elementor development is Elementor build work done by an outside team and delivered as your agency's own. We treat Elementor as a development platform: components the editor lacks become custom widgets, and every page follows one style system.

  • Custom widgets in a plugin. Each widget has its own controls, so editors change text and images while spacing and structure stay fixed.
  • Global styles from your Figma. Colours, fonts and spacing are set once as globals, replacing per-section overrides.
  • Containers instead of nested sections. Flexbox containers produce less markup than the old section and column layouts, which helps pages load faster.
  • Theme builder templates. Headers, footers, archives, single templates and popups, with every display condition written into the handover.
  • Editor limits. Elementor's role manager can restrict the client's team to content, so the layout is harder to break.

Fixing a slow or inconsistent Elementor site

An audit tells you whether a cleanup or a rebuild costs less, and you get that answer in writing before you quote your client. Most audits work through the same checklist:

  • Count the add-on packs and the widgets actually in use, then switch off the rest.
  • Replace local colour and font overrides with global styles.
  • Convert old section and column layouts to containers where it cuts markup.
  • Size images for each breakpoint and lazy-load anything below the first screen.
  • Check that Elementor's CSS output and the caching plugin work together.
  • Remove leftover templates, unused fonts and old revisions from the page and the database.

Where speed is the main complaint, our performance optimisation service measures Core Web Vitals on real devices before and after. Where the site is broken, website rescue and bug fixing finds the cause first.

How Elementor projects run with your agency

A named producer runs each Elementor project in your shared Slack Connect or WhatsApp channel, on a staging site under your brand. Our founder has nine years of PHP, WordPress, WooCommerce and Elementor work for agencies in the UK and Bangladesh. The team knows where Elementor builds tend to go wrong.

The team works from Dhaka (UTC+6), so you can brief us at 5pm London and review at 9am. At handover, your client gets an editing guide in your brand that shows which parts they can change. Elementor is one of several approaches in our white-label WordPress development service.

What Elementor work costs

Elementor builds are WordPress builds, so every monthly plan covers them. Essential starts from £500 a month, for 1 active project and up to 5 pages per project. A cleanup, a widget library or a build outside your plan gets its own written scope and fixed price.

Elementor Pro and add-on licences are billed at cost or held in your account. See every plan on our rates page.

Questions agencies ask about white-label Elementor development

Do you need Elementor Pro?

For most agency builds, yes. Theme builder templates, popups, global widgets and content-only editing in the role manager all need Pro.

The licence sits in your account or the client's, billed at cost, so it stays with the site after handover. Simple single pages can run on the free version, and the scope says which one we assume.

Can our client still break the design?

It becomes much harder. Custom widgets expose only the controls the design allows, and global styles keep colours and fonts in one place.

The role manager can limit editors to content, and the editing guide shows your client what to change. If a scoped feature breaks after launch, we fix it at our cost.

Do you use third-party add-on packs?

Only when one does the job well and is actively maintained. Large add-on packs load code for dozens of widgets when a site uses only a few.

We usually build the missing piece as a custom widget instead. Any add-on we do use is listed in the handover with its licence holder.

Can you build our Figma design in Elementor?

Yes. We set up global colours, fonts and spacing from your Figma first, then build reusable sections and templates.

Each page is compared with your frames before you see it. Anything Elementor cannot reproduce cleanly is flagged in the scope, with a custom widget or a small design change suggested.

Will the client see your name in Elementor?

No. The custom widget plugin, saved templates and documentation carry your agency's name, and there is no credit link on the site.

We never contact your client. Logins come through a shared vault with the least access the work needs, and we remove that access at handover.

As a headless WordPress development agency, we split your client's site in two. WordPress stays where editors write and publish, and a Next.js front end renders what visitors see. You sell the build, and we deliver it under your brand.

What a headless WordPress development agency builds for you

WordPress becomes the content source and Next.js becomes the website. The two talk through the REST API or WPGraphQL, and visitors never touch the WordPress install.

  • ACF field groups designed per template, so each page type has the fields it needs and nothing more.
  • Menus, settings and custom post types exposed to the front end, with only public data leaving WordPress.
  • Draft preview links that show unpublished changes on the real Next.js front end.
  • On-demand revalidation, so a published edit replaces the cached page without a full deploy.
  • Forms and integrations sent through Next.js route handlers, so the browser never calls WordPress.

Headless WordPress is one of several stacks we offer under white-label Next.js development, alongside Payload, Sanity and Postgres apps.

When headless is the right call, and when it is not

Headless suits a client whose WordPress site keeps failing Core Web Vitals or needs interactions a page builder cannot deliver. It is the wrong choice for some briefs, and the scope will say so.

Good fit: marketing teams happy in the WordPress admin, sites with heavy custom design, and clients who care about speed on mobile.

Poor fit: clients who expect drag-and-drop layouts, or who rely on plugins that output front-end HTML, such as page builders and sliders.

If a client only needs a faster WordPress site, a performance pass may solve it for less. We will tell you that before you sell a rebuild.

Builds you can inspect

The Bulk Bag Man runs on this pattern. A WordPress child theme exposes ACF fields, menus and a Supplies post type through the REST API. A Next.js App Router front end renders it on Vercel.

Contact form submissions pass through a route handler, so the browser never talks to WordPress directly. The client still edits everything in the WordPress admin they already know.

This website, softvoltai.com, works the same way: headless WordPress with a Next.js front end on Vercel. The page you are reading is managed in WordPress.

Pricing and how a project runs

Headless Next.js builds are included from the Growth plan (from £1,200/month). It covers up to 3 active projects, up to 10 pages per project and priority turnaround of 7 to 10 business days. Larger rebuilds get their own fixed-price scope, and every plan is listed on our rates page.

Each build runs on a password-protected staging URL under your brand, with a named producer in your shared channel. On a rebuild, we carry over metadata, sitemaps, structured data and redirects, and can work alongside your technical SEO specialist.

Questions agencies ask about headless WordPress

Will the client's editors notice a difference?

Mostly in speed. They log in to the same WordPress admin and edit fields set up for each template. Page-builder layouts no longer apply, because Next.js renders the front end.

We include an editing guide in your brand that shows where each field appears on the site.

Which plugins still work on a headless site?

Plugins that work in the admin or on data keep working, including ACF, SEO plugins that store metadata, and custom post type plugins. Plugins that output front-end HTML, such as page builders and sliders, do not.

We list every plugin in the scope and say what replaces each one.

Is headless WordPress good for SEO?

It can be. Next.js renders pages on the server, so search engines receive complete HTML. We set metadata, canonical tags, XML sitemaps and structured data in the front end, and carry over redirects on a rebuild.

We cannot promise rankings, but a fast, well-structured front end removes technical problems that hold a site back.

Where is the site hosted?

The Next.js front end runs on Vercel by default, or on your client's own infrastructure. WordPress stays on its existing host or moves to a new one, and it no longer serves visitors directly. Hosting is billed at cost or held in your accounts, and we never mark it up.

Can you convert an existing WordPress site to headless?

Yes. We audit the current theme, plugins and URLs first, then scope the rebuild at a fixed price. Content usually stays where it is, so editors keep their posts and pages.

We map every old URL to the new front end and set redirects wherever anything moves.

services.heading: Internal tools and dashboards for agencies
services.seo_description: Internal tools development for agency clients: Next.js and PostgreSQL apps that replace the spreadsheet, with roles, audit trail and exports. Get a scope.
services.intro: We take on internal tools development for agencies whose clients have outgrown a spreadsheet. We build quoting tools, job boards, stock trackers and approval flows in Next.js on PostgreSQL, delivered under your brand.
services.content_html:
Internal tools development means building the small private application a client's team uses every day, such as a quote builder or a job tracker. We build it under your agency's brand, and the client owns the code, the data and the hosting account at handover.

When internal tools development beats the spreadsheet

A custom tool pays off when the spreadsheet starts causing mistakes the business can count. Common signs are wrong prices on quotes, jobs lost between tabs and a sheet only one person understands.

It also pays off when different people need different views. A spreadsheet struggles to hide margins from a sales rep or show who changed a price last Tuesday.

Dashboards come in here too. When the tool holds the data, the numbers the team checks each morning sit on the same database, so nobody reconciles two versions.

Build, buy or keep the spreadsheet

We will tell you when a build is the wrong answer. Our advice depends on the situation:

SituationOur advice
Off-the-shelf software fits the process with small compromisesBuy it, and connect it to the client's other tools with workflow automation
One or two people use the sheet and the data is not sensitiveKeep the spreadsheet, and add validation and protected ranges
Several people edit it, roles matter, or it holds customer dataBuild an internal tool with roles and an audit trail
Customers or suppliers need to log in tooBuild a portal, covered by our Next.js apps on PostgreSQL service

What we build into every tool

Every tool gets roles, an audit trail, careful imports, exports and tested backups. These details decide whether the team still trusts it a year later:

  • Roles designed with the client: who can see costs, who can approve and who can only add records
  • An audit trail: every change recorded with the person and the time, so a disputed edit can be traced
  • Imports that expect real spreadsheets: merged cells, duplicate rows and dates typed as text are caught in a validation report before anything is written
  • Exports to CSV: the client's data is never trapped in the tool
  • Backups with a tested restore: we prove the backup works before the team relies on it

By default, tools run on Vercel with a managed PostgreSQL database, in an account the client owns. Email notifications go out through Resend from the client's own domain.

Pricing, ownership and support

Each tool starts with a half-day scoping workshop and a written spec with screens. You then get a fixed price, and nothing starts until you approve it. If you run several builds at once, compare the monthly plans on our rates page.

At handover the repository transfers to you or your client, with training notes and a maintenance plan. We revoke our access and confirm it in writing, as our security page describes.

Some tools need a step that reads free text, such as supplier emails. That part is scoped under our white-label AI automation service.

Questions agencies ask about internal tools development

How long does an internal tool take to build?

Weeks rather than months for a tightly scoped tool, and the written scope fixes the exact timeline before work starts. The scoping workshop keeps the first version small: the screens the team needs every day, not every idea from the first meeting. Further features follow as fixed-price changes once the team has used it.

Who owns the code and the data?

Your client does, or your agency if that is how you sell it. The repository transfers at handover, the database and hosting sit in an account the client controls, and every record can be exported to CSV. Staging sites are removed within 14 days of launch unless you ask otherwise.

Can it import the client's existing spreadsheet?

Yes, and we plan for messy data. The import runs against validation rules first and reports the rows it could not read, such as duplicates, missing fields or dates typed as text. The client fixes those rows or agrees a mapping with us, and only then does the data go live.

Where is the tool hosted?

On Vercel with a managed PostgreSQL database by default, in an account your client owns. If the client has its own infrastructure or rules on where data lives, we deploy there instead and note it in the scope. Hosting is billed at cost or held in their account, with no mark-up.

What happens when the client's process changes?

It will, and the tool should change with it. Small changes fit inside a monthly plan or a maintenance arrangement, and larger ones are quoted as a fixed-price change with a written scope. Defects inside the agreed scope after launch are fixed at our cost, whatever their size.

services.heading: White-label landing page development
services.seo_description: White-label landing page development for agencies: fast Next.js or WordPress campaign pages, ad tracking tested before launch. Get a fixed price first.
services.intro: Our white-label landing page development gives your paid campaigns fast mobile pages, with conversion tracking tested before traffic arrives. We build them on Next.js or as a lean WordPress template under your brand, with a structure your team can clone for the next campaign.
services.content_html:
What white-label landing page development includes

White-label landing page development means an outside team builds the campaign pages your agency sells, under your brand. We build the page and the measurement around it, and your team keeps the strategy, the ad accounts and the client.

The page is half the job. The other half is making sure Google Ads, Meta and GA4 agree on what happened:

  • UTM parameters and click IDs (gclid, fbclid) captured in hidden form fields, so the client's CRM knows which campaign produced each lead.
  • One conversion per submission, with no duplicates when a visitor refreshes the thank-you page.
  • Consent Mode v2 defaults set before any tag fires, with each consent state tested.
  • Message match, so the headline and offer on each variant follow the ad group that sends traffic to it.
  • Spam protection on every form that adds no friction for real visitors.

Next.js or WordPress for campaign pages

Use Next.js when page speed and the number of variants matter most. Use WordPress when the client's team wants to edit the page themselves.

Campaign needApproachWhy
High paid spend and several variantsNext.js on VercelPages are pre-rendered and served from a global network, so mobile loads stay quick
The client's team edits copy every weekA lean WordPress template without a page builderA familiar admin, with only the fields the page needs
The client already runs a headless siteA new route in the existing Next.js appThe same design system and deploy, with no second platform

Forms on Next.js pages post through a server route handler, so the browser never talks to the CMS or the CRM directly. Our founder used the same pattern on The Bulk Bag Man, a headless WordPress build with a Next.js front end.

Tracking checklist before traffic goes live

No campaign should send traffic to a page whose conversions nobody has tested. Before launch, we check that:

  • each form and call button fires the GA4 key event and the ad platform conversion once
  • Google Ads conversions, and enhanced conversions where the account uses them, line up with the GA4 count
  • Meta Pixel and Conversions API events deduplicate correctly
  • consent banner choices change what fires, on mobile and desktop
  • Core Web Vitals hold up on a real mid-range phone, alongside the lab score

For tracking problems across a whole site, see analytics and tracking. For deciding what to test on the page, see conversion rate optimisation.

Pricing and how it fits your campaigns

Landing pages run under your monthly plan like any other build, within its page limit. Essential starts from £500 a month, with up to 5 pages per project. A one-off page or a set of variants outside your plan gets a written scope and fixed price first.

If a campaign starts next week, say so in the brief. We will tell you whether we can hit the date and what it costs. See every plan on our rates page.

Landing pages sit within our white-label web development service, alongside full site builds.

Questions agencies ask about white-label landing page development

How quickly can you build a landing page?

On a plan, turnaround is 10 to 15 business days on Essential, 7 to 10 on Growth and 5 to 7 on Premium. Once a reusable template exists, the next campaign page takes far less time. For a rush, put the date in the brief, and we will either quote what it takes to hit it or tell you we cannot.

Can our team edit the page after launch?

Yes. On WordPress, your team edits the copy, images and form settings in the admin.

On Next.js, the content can come from a headless CMS, so editors change it without a deploy. We can also make the changes for you within your plan. The handover guide shows how to clone the template for the next campaign.

Do you write the landing page copy?

We implement copy and section structure from your brief or Figma, so the words stay with your team and the client. We flag structural problems early, such as an offer buried below the first screen or a form asking for more than the CRM uses. Your strategist decides what changes.

Can you guarantee a higher conversion rate?

No. We build pages that load fast on mobile, keep tracking accurate and make variants easy to test.

Whether a page converts better depends on the offer, the audience and the traffic, which your team controls. Accurate tracking lets you see what works and report it to your client.

Where are the pages hosted?

Next.js pages run on Vercel by default, or on the client's own infrastructure if they prefer. WordPress pages run on the client's existing host.

Hosting accounts sit with your agency or the client and are billed at cost, with no mark-up. The pages stay live whoever maintains them later.

services.heading: White-label Laravel development for agencies
services.seo_description: White-label Laravel development for agencies: custom web apps, portals, APIs and admin panels built under your brand, with a fixed-price scope in 2 days.
services.intro: SoftVolt AI provides white-label Laravel development for agencies whose clients need an application, not another CMS plugin. We build portals, APIs and admin panels under your brand, and your client never hears from us. You get a written scope and a fixed price within two business days.
services.content_html:
Our white-label Laravel development service is for agencies that have sold a client an application rather than a website. We plan the data model and build the app in Laravel. It comes back with your name on the code, the staging site and every document.

Nothing starts until you approve a written, fixed-price scope. We sign a mutual NDA before you share client details, and a named producer runs the project in your shared channel.

What is white-label Laravel development?

White-label Laravel development means an outside team builds a Laravel application that your agency delivers to its client as its own work. The developers stay invisible: no credit in the code, no contact with your client, and documents in your brand. Agencies use it to take on application briefs without hiring a PHP team.

Laravel is a PHP framework with authentication, queues, scheduled tasks and database migrations built in. It suits clients whose process needs custom rules, user roles and reporting, especially when their hosting or developers already run PHP.

What a white-label Laravel partner handles for your agency

We handle the application from data model to deployment. The deliverables list covers the outputs; these are the parts that decide whether the app survives its first year.

  • Custom web apps and portals. Customer portals, supplier portals, quoting tools and booking systems, with every user role mapped before the first migration is written.
  • APIs. REST or JSON APIs for a mobile app, a Next.js front end or a WordPress site. Token authentication and versioned routes stop a change from breaking a live app.
  • Admin panels. Screens for the client's staff to manage records, approve requests and export data. Permissions are checked on the server, never only hidden in the interface.
  • Queues and scheduled jobs. Emails, imports, PDF generation and third-party syncs run in the background with retries and failure alerts, so a slow API never freezes a page.
  • Testing. Feature tests cover the flows that cost money if they break, such as sign-up, payment, approval and export. Tests run before every deploy.
  • Existing Laravel apps. We take over apps another developer built. A short audit comes first, then upgrades, fixes or new features against a fixed price.

You stay in charge of the client, the scope and the price you charge them. When the client asks for a change mid-build, we write it down and price it before anyone builds it.

We raise the awkward details early, such as who can delete a record or what happens to a booking when a payment fails. The answers go into the scope, not into a support ticket six months later.

Which Laravel approach fits which client

The front end decides most of the approach. Pick by who uses the app and how interactive it needs to feel; the written scope confirms the choice.

Client needApproachWhy
Staff admin panel with forms, tables and filtersLaravel with Blade and LivewireServer-rendered screens with live updates, all in PHP, which keeps maintenance simple.
An app that should feel like a single-page appLaravel with Inertia and React or VueLaravel keeps routing, auth and validation while the front end behaves like a modern app.
A mobile app or separate front end needs dataLaravel as an API onlyOne back end serves the app, the website and any partner integrations.
Business logic beside an existing WordPress siteCustom WordPress pluginThe logic stays inside the CMS the client already runs and pays for.
A small tool that replaces a spreadsheetInternal toolScoped tightly and built in weeks, with auth, exports and backups included.

Laravel or Next.js

Choose Laravel when the client's hosting, developers or existing code are PHP, or when the app is mostly admin screens, reports and background jobs.

Choose a Next.js web app on PostgreSQL when the front end is React, the marketing site runs on Next.js or future developers will write TypeScript. Both handle auth, roles and payments well, so the deciding factor is usually who maintains the app after handover.

How a Laravel project runs with an agency

Every project starts with a written scope that lists user roles, flows, the data model and each integration. You approve it before we write any code.

Work runs on a password-protected staging URL under your brand, with a named producer in a shared Slack Connect or WhatsApp channel. The team is in Dhaka (UTC+6, no daylight saving): our afternoon overlaps the UK working day and our evening overlaps US East Coast mornings.

You see working features as they land. Each milestone goes to staging with seeded test data, so you can click through the flows before your client does.

Before handover, the build goes through our published QA checklist. The handover includes deployment notes, environment settings and an admin guide in your brand.

Pricing for Laravel work

Most Laravel applications are scoped as one-off projects with a fixed price, sent within two business days of the brief. Monthly plans and what each one includes are on our rates page.

If Laravel work recurs, the scope confirms whether it fits a plan. Premium (from £2,400/month) covers builds alongside AI automation, SEO and paid media, with up to 6 active projects. Enterprise is quoted and covers the full white-label suite, with turnaround agreed in writing.

These factors move the price of a one-off scope most:

  • the number of user roles and the permission rules between them
  • integrations with payment providers, CRMs, accounting software or other external APIs
  • data migration from spreadsheets or a legacy system
  • reports and exports the client's staff rely on every week
  • the state of the code, if we are taking over an existing app

Hosting and third-party services are billed at cost or held in your accounts. We never mark them up.

Builds you can open

None of our public case studies is a Laravel application. They are sites our founder delivered before SoftVolt AI, and white-label partner work never appears without the agency's written permission.

The closest in shape are PHP builds with business logic and enquiry flows. Patriot Insurance Group was a full-stack build for a division of a US insurance group, with a services architecture and quote-request flows.

Ascent Energy was a UK energy e-commerce platform, scoped, built and project managed through to launch.

If you want to judge our Laravel work first, send one small brief. You get a fixed price, and you decide on the next project after you have seen the code.

Dedicated Laravel developer, freelancer or white-label partner

A white-label partner suits agencies whose Laravel work arrives in projects rather than as a steady full-time load. If you have enough application work to fill a role every month, a hire may be the better choice.

What mattersDedicated in-house hireFreelancerWhite-label partner
CostSalary plus benefits, payroll taxes, equipment and your management timeAn hourly or project rate that varies widely, plus your time checking the workA fixed price against a written scope, or a monthly plan
Time to startWeeks to months to advertise, interview and onboardWhenever someone good happens to be freeA written scope and fixed price within two business days

Holidays and sick daysDelivery pausesYou find a replacement mid-projectTeam cover, with the same producer on the thread

If it does not work outNotice periods, redundancy and a new searchLost time and a scramble to recover files and loginsWork ends at handover, with documentation and credentials returned

Your client stays yours

We work behind your agency and nowhere else. The protection terms are signed once and cover every project after.

  • A mutual NDA, on our template or yours, before you share a client's name.
  • No contact with your client: no emails, no LinkedIn and no portfolio use without your written permission.
  • No credit in the code, the admin panel or the footer. Commits, staging domains and documents carry your brand.
  • Server, database and third-party credentials stay in a shared vault with least-privilege access. We revoke our access at handover and confirm it in writing.
  • For personal data, we work under UK GDPR (IDTA or UK Addendum), EU Standard Contractual Clauses and an Article 28 data processing agreement.

Read exactly how client data is handled on our security page.

For UK, US, Canadian and Australian agencies

For UK agencies

Our afternoon overlaps your working day, so questions about a data model or a failing job get answered while your team is at their desks. Brief us at 5pm London and review at 9am. Plans are priced in pounds, and personal data is handled under UK GDPR with the IDTA or UK Addendum.

For US, Canadian and Australian agencies

Our evening overlaps East Coast mornings in the US and Canada, and our morning overlaps the Sydney afternoon. That gives you a live window for calls and an overnight build cycle for everything else. You sign the same NDA and protection terms as a UK agency.

Questions agencies ask about white-label Laravel development

Is this the same as a Laravel developer for hire?

No. A developer for hire usually bills time and leaves you to manage the work. We quote a fixed price against a written scope, and a named producer runs the project in your shared channel.

You still decide what gets built. You simply do not have to supervise each task.

Can we have a dedicated Laravel developer for one client?

For ongoing work, a monthly plan gives you a named producer who knows the app, plus team cover for holidays. Changes are scoped and scheduled through your shared channel rather than through a developer sitting inside your agency. If the work is a single build, a fixed-price project is usually the simpler route.

Why outsource Laravel development rather than hire?

Many agencies do not have enough Laravel work to keep a full-time developer busy every month. Outsourcing turns that cost into a fixed price per project or a monthly plan, with a team behind it rather than one person. When your application pipeline is steady enough to fill a role, hiring may make more sense.

Can you take over a Laravel app another developer built?

Yes. We start with a short audit covering Laravel and PHP versions, dependencies, test coverage, queues, hosting and known bugs.

You get a written summary and a fixed-price scope for the upgrade, fixes or new features. If the app needs urgent fixes first, we scope those separately so the client is not waiting on a full review.

Do you write automated tests?

Yes. Feature tests cover the flows that would cost the client money if they broke, such as sign-up, payments, approvals and exports.

Tests run before each deploy. If you need a set coverage target or your own CI setup, put it in the brief and we will include it in the scope.

Where will the app be hosted?

Wherever suits the client, whether that is their existing server or a cloud host we agree in the scope. We set up deployment, queue workers, scheduled tasks and backups, then document the setup in a runbook. Hosting is billed at cost or held in your or your client's account.

Who owns the code?

Your agency, or your client if that is your agreement with them. We transfer the repository at handover, with environment notes and an admin guide in your brand. Our access to servers and services is then revoked, and we confirm the removal in writing.

Can Laravel work alongside the client's WordPress site?

Yes. A common pattern keeps marketing pages in WordPress and runs the logged-in app on Laravel, often on a subdomain.

We can also build a Laravel API that a WordPress or Next.js site reads from. The scope sets out which system owns which data, so nothing is stored twice.

What do you need from us to quote?

A description of who uses the app and what they need to do, plus any spreadsheets, existing code or screenshots of the current process. Tell us about integrations and deadlines. We reply within one business day and send a written scope with a fixed price within two business days.

services.heading: White-label local SEO services
services.seo_description: White-label local SEO for agencies: Google Business Profile, citations, location pages and an honest review process. Get a fixed-price scope in two days.
services.intro: Our white-label local SEO service helps your multi-location and service-area clients show up in map results and local searches, under your agency's brand. We work on Google Business Profiles, citations, location pages and the review process, then report each location's visibility in your format.
services.content_html:
What white-label local SEO includes

White-label local SEO is the work that helps a client appear in map results and local searches, carried out by a partner under your agency's brand. For most local clients it comes down to the Google Business Profile, consistent citations, useful location pages and a steady review process.

Google weighs relevance, distance and prominence for local results. Distance depends on where the searcher stands, which no agency controls, so our work focuses on relevance and prominence.

Google Business Profile, citations and location pages

Google Business Profile

We audit each profile against the real business: primary and secondary categories, services, hours, service areas, photos and the website link. Website links get UTM tags so GA4 can separate profile visits from other organic traffic.

The client keeps ownership of every profile. We work as a manager you add, never as an owner.

Citations

Business name, address and phone number should match everywhere the business is listed. We audit the main directories in the client's country, fix inconsistent or duplicate listings, and keep a citation sheet that becomes the source of truth for future changes.

Location pages

Each location or service-area page needs content that belongs to that place: the team, the services offered there, local proof and how to get there. Pages that only swap the town name count as doorway pages under Google's spam policies. We build to a template you approve and fill it with real local detail.

A review process without shortcuts

Reviews come from real customers through a simple, repeatable process. We set up the request flow, usually an email or text with a direct review link after each job, and write response templates in the client's voice for positive and negative reviews.

We never write, buy or incentivise reviews. Fake reviews break Google's policies, and in the UK and US they break consumer protection law too. Google's policies also rule out asking only happy customers, so every customer gets the same request.

How it runs, and what it costs

You send the list of locations, the client's goals and access to the profiles and site. We return a written scope and a fixed price within two business days, then work to a monthly plan. The monthly local visibility report goes out in your brand, with a change log for each location.

Our team in Dhaka (UTC+6) overlaps the UK working day in our afternoon and US East Coast mornings in our evening.

Ongoing local SEO sits within the Premium plan, from £2,400 a month, and Enterprise, which adds multi-brand and multi-team support. A one-off citation clean-up or a set of location pages gets its own fixed price, and the number of locations moves that cost most. Every plan is on the rates page.

Local work is one part of our white-label SEO services. For a build you can open, see SEO Agency in Essex, an agency site our founder built before SoftVolt AI, with service and location page templates the agency extends itself.

Questions agencies ask about white-label local SEO

Do you guarantee a place in the map pack?

No. Map results change with the searcher's location, so the same search shows different results a few streets apart.

Google also weighs prominence signals such as reviews and links, which build over time. We commit to the work in the scope and report visibility honestly, including the areas where the client is weaker.

Who owns the Google Business Profile?

The client does, always. We ask to be added as a manager, which lets us edit the profile without control over ownership or other users.

If a former supplier or an ex-employee owns a profile, we help you through Google's ownership request process. Our access ends at handover, as set out on our security page.

How do you handle clients with many locations?

We keep one location sheet as the source of truth for names, addresses, phone numbers, hours and categories. Profiles, citations and pages are checked against it, so a change at one branch reaches everywhere. Location pages carry LocalBusiness structured data, handled with our technical SEO work, and reports break visibility down by location.

Can you help a service-area business with no shopfront?

Yes. The profile hides the address and lists the areas served instead, which is what Google expects for businesses that visit their customers. Service-area pages then explain what the client offers in each area with real detail, such as jobs completed there, rather than repeating one page with a new town name.

Will you post reviews to get a new client started?

No. We will not buy reviews, swap them or write them for staff to post. Fake reviews break Google's policies and consumer protection law in the UK and US, and they can get a profile suspended.

A new client gets a review request process as part of onboarding, so genuine reviews start building straight away.

services.heading: White-label Meta Ads management
services.seo_description: White-label Meta Ads management for agencies: Facebook and Instagram campaigns, Pixel and Conversions API, reported in your brand. See how it runs.
services.intro: Our white-label Meta Ads management runs Facebook and Instagram campaigns for your clients under your agency's brand. We set up the Pixel and Conversions API properly, test creative to a written plan and report monthly in your template, while your client keeps ownership of every ad account and asset.
services.content_html:
What white-label Meta Ads management covers

White-label Meta Ads management means a partner runs your clients' Facebook and Instagram campaigns while your agency presents the work as its own. We handle campaign structure, audiences, ad copy, creative testing and measurement. You keep the strategy, the budget approvals and every conversation with the client.

The client's assets stay with the client. Their business portfolio shares the ad account, Page, Instagram account and dataset with your agency's portfolio as a partner, and we work through the access your portfolio gives us. We do not hold Meta Business Partner status.

Measurement comes first

Since Apple's App Tracking Transparency arrived with iOS 14.5, the Meta Pixel on its own misses a share of conversions. The Conversions API closes much of that gap by sending the same events from the server, so we set up both and verify them before spend scales.

That means matching event IDs so Meta counts each conversion once, checking Event Match Quality in Events Manager and respecting consent choices for UK and EU visitors. Our analytics and tracking team handles the server side on the client's platform.

Creative testing with a plan

Each test changes one thing: the hook, the format, the offer or the audience. Every ad gets enough budget and time for a fair read, and results go into a test log, so the next round starts from what the account has already learned.

We write the ad copy and the test plan. Tell us in the brief who supplies images and video, whether that is the client, your designers or a production partner. Winning ads move into the main campaigns, and tired creative is replaced before frequency climbs too high.

For lead generation, we compare Meta's instant forms with sending traffic to a landing page, because instant forms can bring more leads of lower quality. If the landing page is the weak point, our developers build high-speed landing pages matched to each ad set.

How it runs, and what it costs

services.intro: A white-label Core Web Vitals optimisation service for agencies whose clients fail in Search Console or pay for slow landing pages. We fix what slows real visitors down, then show the before and after with field data your client can check.
services.content_html:
Our Core Web Vitals optimisation service fixes the speed and stability problems that real visitors feel, and your agency delivers the result under its own brand. We start from field data, because a perfect Lighthouse score on a fast laptop says little about a mid-range phone on mobile data.

What our Core Web Vitals optimisation service fixes

Core Web Vitals has three measures, and a page passes when 75% of real visits meet each threshold. Search Console reports them from 28 days of visitor data.

MetricWhat it measuresGoodFixes we usually make
LCP (Largest Contentful Paint)How fast the main content appears2.5 seconds or lessServer response, image size and priority, render-blocking CSS and fonts
INP (Interaction to Next Paint)How quickly the page responds to taps and clicks200 milliseconds or lessHeavy JavaScript, third-party scripts, slow sliders, menus and page-builder widgets
CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift)How much the layout jumps while loading0.1 or lessImage dimensions, reserved space for banners and embeds, font loading

We test on throttled mobile profiles in PageSpeed Insights and WebPageTest, then confirm the change in field data. That way the report your client sees matches what their customers experience.

Why stacked speed plugins make sites slower

Several caching and optimisation plugins on one site often fight each other, because each one rewrites the same CSS and JavaScript. We remove the overlap first, then pick one approach and configure it properly.

On WordPress that usually means one caching layer such as WP Rocket, Cloudflare in front of the host, images in modern formats at the right size, and fonts served locally. On Elementor sites we switch off unused widgets and their assets. On WooCommerce we keep cart, checkout and account pages out of the page cache, so speed gains never break orders.

Third-party scripts are often where most of the delay comes from, and they need a client conversation. Chat widgets, heatmaps and forgotten tracking tags each cost load time. We list every script, what it does and who owns it, so you and the client can agree which ones stay.

When the build itself is the limit

Some sites cannot pass on their current build, however much tuning they get. Heavy themes, deeply nested page-builder sections and slow shared hosting all set a ceiling.

When we reach that ceiling, we say so in writing and give you options. A hosting change through our website migration service may be enough.

If it is not, a rebuilt template or a headless WordPress front end in Next.js keeps editors in WordPress while visitors get a faster site. For paid traffic, a separate high-speed landing page is often the fastest route.

What you get back, proof and pricing

You get a before-and-after report in your template with lab results and field data side by side.

Faster pages help visitors and the landing page side of Google Ads Quality Score, but we never promise a ranking change. Speed is one signal among many, and our technical SEO implementation handles the rest of an audit.

For a build you can test yourself, open the SEO Agency in Essex case study. Our founder built it before SoftVolt AI, with speed treated as a requirement rather than a plugin added at the end.

A performance audit and fix sprint gets a fixed price within two business days of the brief, and the rates page shows the monthly plans. This service is part of our white-label web development work.

Questions agencies ask about Core Web Vitals

How long until Search Console shows a pass?

Search Console reports Core Web Vitals from 28 days of real visitor data, so a fix shipped today shows its full effect about four weeks later. Pages with little traffic may not have their own data and get grouped with similar pages. We confirm each fix in lab tests on release day and track the field data until it settles.

Will better Core Web Vitals improve rankings?

We cannot promise that, and nobody honestly can. Core Web Vitals is one of many signals Google uses, and content and links usually weigh more.

Faster pages do keep more visitors on the page, which matters most on paid landing pages. We report what changed in speed and leave ranking claims out.

Do you change the design to make a site faster?

Only with your approval. Most fixes are invisible: image formats, caching, script loading and font handling.

When a design element is the cost, such as an autoplaying video hero or a heavy slider, we show what it costs in seconds and suggest lighter versions. You decide what to put to the client.

Can you speed up a WooCommerce store without breaking checkout?

Yes. We exclude cart, checkout and account pages from the page cache and test every change on staging first.

Before release we place test orders with each live payment method, on mobile and desktop. Nothing goes live until checkout passes, and large stores also get a database clean-up.

Do you optimise Next.js sites as well as WordPress?

Yes. On Next.js we look at image and font handling, how much JavaScript ships to the browser, third-party script loading and server response times on Vercel or the client's host. The goal is the same as on WordPress: a pass in field data your client can check in Search Console themselves.

Webflow suits marketing sites edited by non-developers, where the design matters and the content model is simple. WordPress suits sites that need complex plugins, larger stores or custom business logic.

If a messy Webflow site needs a clean rebuild, we audit its classes and collections first, then scope the rebuild at a fixed price. Webflow sits within our white-label web development service, alongside WordPress, Shopify and Next.js.

Pricing
