Webflow site plans and workspace seats stay in your or the client's account, and we never mark them up. Compare the monthly plans for ongoing work on our rates page.

Questions agencies ask about white-label Webflow development

Do you build in our Webflow workspace?

Yes, or in the client's. We join as a workspace member with the access the job needs, build there and leave when the site is handed over.

Your agency stays the name on the project, and we confirm in writing when our access is removed.

Can the client edit the site without breaking it?

Yes, within the limits we set. Editors work on CMS content and text in the Webflow Editor, while layout and classes stay with designers. We hand over an editing guide in your brand that shows what each person can change and what stays locked.

Can you match our prototype's interactions?

Usually, yes. We rebuild interactions with Webflow's native tools first and use custom JavaScript only where they fall short. Each interaction is tested on real phones and desktop browsers.

If one would hurt performance or accessibility, we suggest an alternative before building it.

Do you set up SEO and tracking?

Yes. We set titles, meta descriptions, Open Graph images and clean URLs for each template, plus CMS fields so editors can manage them. Forms, analytics and tracking are connected and tested before launch.

We do not guarantee rankings, but the site launches with the technical basics in place.

Can you take over a Webflow site another developer built?

Yes. We audit the class structure, CMS collections and interactions, then tell you whether to tidy it or rebuild it. You get a fixed-price scope for either option.

Most messy Webflow sites suffer from one-off classes, which a documented class system fixes.

services.heading: White-label website maintenance plans
services.seo_description: White-label website maintenance for agencies: staged updates, off-site backups, uptime monitoring and a monthly report in your brand. See what's covered.
services.intro: Our white-label website maintenance gives your agency a care plan to resell on every client site. We stage and test updates, keep nightly off-site backups, watch uptime and send a monthly report in your brand.
services.content_html:
White-label website maintenance means we look after your clients' sites while your agency sells the care plan as its own. The reports carry your logo, and we never contact your client.

What white-label website maintenance covers

It covers the routine work that keeps a site safe and working, plus a small block of hours for fixes each month. The value lies in how carefully that routine is done.

Updates are the clearest example. A plugin update can break a checkout or a form without any error on screen. So we apply updates on staging first, test the pages and flows that earn the client money, then release them.

PHP upgrades get the same treatment, because hosts retire old PHP versions on their own schedule. We also check backups by restoring them, since a backup nobody has tested is a guess.

Sites that need more than updates

WooCommerce stores need the most care. We test the checkout after updates, and payment gateway plugins get extra caution because a silent failure costs sales.

Restoring a store also needs thought. Rolling back the whole database would delete orders placed since the backup. So we plan a store restore around the order data instead of running it blind.

Shopify and Webflow sites have no plugin updates in the WordPress sense. Care there means reviewing apps and integrations, checking forms and tracking, and handling content fixes from the monthly hours.

A site that is already broken, slow or hacked needs work before a plan can start. We scope that separately through website rescue and bug fixing, performance optimisation or our WordPress malware cleanup service.

A store our founder built and maintained

Our founder built the Heat Pumps 4 Pools WooCommerce store for a UK pool-heating retailer: catalogue, product templates and checkout. After launch he stayed on as its maintenance engineer.

That ongoing maintenance is the same care-plan pattern we now offer agencies under their own brand. The store is live, so you can open it and judge the work yourself.

Pricing a care plan

Maintenance is ongoing work, so it runs on a monthly retainer sized in hours. You get a written scope listing each site and what it covers before anything starts. Plan prices start from £500 a month, and our rates page lists what each tier includes.

The number of sites, how many are WooCommerce stores and the fix hours you want each month move the price most. Premium plugin licences, backup storage and CDN costs are billed at cost or held in your accounts.

What you charge your client is up to you. Your margin is never our business.

Questions agencies ask about white-label website maintenance

Will the monthly report carry our brand?

Yes. Each site gets a monthly report in your agency's brand, listing the updates applied, backup and uptime status, fixes made and anything we recommend. You send it to the client as your own work.

Staging domains and handover documents carry your brand too, and nothing in the report mentions us.

Do you maintain sites you did not build?

Yes. We begin with a short audit of the theme, plugins, hosting and backups, and flag anything that needs fixing before routine maintenance makes sense. That audit becomes part of the written scope, so you and your client both see the starting point.

Fixes it turns up are quoted separately.

What happens if an update breaks something?

Updates go to staging first, so a break shows up there rather than on the live site. If something breaks on the live site anyway, we roll back from the latest backup and fix the cause on staging. Where the fault sits inside the agreed scope, the fix is at our cost, and the monthly report records what happened.

Who holds the hosting and plugin licences?

You or your client, never us. We work through a scoped login shared from a password vault, and licences stay in the account that pays for them. If the plan ends, we revoke our access and confirm it in writing, as set out in our security practices.

Is malware cleanup included in a care plan?

Prevention is included: hardening, malware scanning and login protection run on every site in the plan. Cleaning a site that is already infected is a separate fixed-price job, because the time it takes depends on how deep the infection goes. Once the site is clean, it moves onto the plan.

services.heading: Website migration without losing SEO
services.seo_description: A white-label website migration service for agencies: redirect maps, URL and metadata parity, staging rehearsal and Search Console checks. See the plan.
services.intro: Our website migration service moves client sites to a new host, platform or domain while protecting rankings and orders. We map every URL, rehearse the move on staging and watch Search Console after launch, all under your agency's brand.
services.content_html:
A website migration service protects what a site has already earned when it moves: search visibility, inbound links, tracking and the client's email. We run the move as your agency's back-room team, with a checklist your client can read and your name on every document.

Lost traffic after a migration usually comes from a few avoidable mistakes. Redirects go missing, titles change, a staging noindex stays in place or tracking never comes across. Our process is built to catch each of them before launch.

What a website migration service has to protect

Each kind of move puts different things at risk, so the plan starts by naming the move.

MoveWhat can go wrongWhat we check
New host, same domain and URLsLost DNS or email records, PHP version differences, missing scheduled tasksFull DNS export, lowered TTL before cutover, MX and SPF records, PHP version, cron
Domain changeRankings drop if redirects or Search Console are mishandledOne-to-one 301s from every old URL, the Change of Address tool, the old domain kept renewed
Platform change, such as Shopify to WooCommerceNew URL patterns, lost product or customer data, dropped metadataURL mapping by pattern and by page, record counts compared, metadata carried over
Redesign on new URLsMerged or removed pages with no redirect, internal links pointing at old URLsA signed-off redirect map, internal links updated, no redirect chains

Redirect mapping and URL parity

Every URL with traffic, links or rankings gets a mapped destination before launch. We build the list from a full crawl, the XML sitemaps, Search Console, analytics landing pages and the pages other sites link to.

  • Redirects are permanent (301) and one-to-one wherever a matching page exists, never a blanket redirect to the home page.
  • Old URLs go straight to their final address, including redirects that already existed before this move.
  • Titles, meta descriptions, headings, canonicals, hreflang and structured data carry across page by page.
  • PDFs and images that rank or attract links get mapped too.

Staging checks before cutover

We rehearse the whole migration on staging before the live move. Staging stays password-protected and set to noindex, and we remove it within 14 days of launch unless you ask otherwise.

Before cutover we crawl staging and compare it with the old site: status codes, metadata, canonicals, internal links and redirects. We test forms, checkout, logins and tracking events end to end, and you sign off. On launch day the most important check is the simplest one: the noindex tag and the staging password are gone from the live site.

Post-launch monitoring in Search Console

After cutover we submit the new sitemap, then watch the Search Console page indexing report and crawl stats for 404s, redirect errors and dropped pages. We compare rankings, organic landing pages and conversions against the pre-launch baseline.

Some movement in the first weeks is normal while Google processes the redirects. We never promise that rankings will hold, but a documented migration removes the avoidable causes of loss.

Pricing and where migration fits

A migration sits outside the monthly plans, so it gets its own written scope and fixed price within two business days of the brief. The rates page explains how one-off scopes and plans fit together. When customer accounts or orders move, we work under the UK IDTA or Addendum and EU SCCs, as our security page explains.

Migration is part of our white-label web development work. SEO agencies can pair it with our technical SEO implementation, and store moves can run alongside WooCommerce development.

Questions agencies ask about website migration

How long do rankings take to settle after a migration?

It depends on the move. A host change that keeps every URL often shows little movement, while a domain or platform change can take several weeks to settle.

We watch Search Console after launch, report what we see, and fix any redirect or indexing fault as soon as it shows up.

Do you handle DNS and the client's email during the move?

We record every DNS record, including MX, SPF and DKIM, before anything changes, and check that email still sends and arrives after cutover. If mailboxes need to move to a new provider, we list that in the scope so nobody assumes it is covered.

How long should the old redirects stay in place?

At least a year, which is Google's own guidance, and longer if old URLs still get links or traffic. For a domain change, the client should keep the old domain renewed, because letting it lapse breaks every redirect and every inbound link pointing at it.

Can you move a WooCommerce store without losing orders?

Yes. We plan cutover for the quietest trading window, freeze product changes for a short period, and run a final sync of orders and customers just before the DNS switch. After launch we place test orders with each payment method and confirm emails, stock levels and order statuses before you tell the client it is done.

A previous migration lost traffic. Can you find out why?

Usually, yes. We rebuild the old URL list from Search Console, archived sitemaps and backlink data, then compare it with the current redirects, metadata and indexing.

Typical findings are missing redirects, redirect chains, changed titles and stray noindex tags. We fix what can be fixed and tell you honestly what is unlikely to recover.

services.heading: Website rescue and bug fixing for agencies
services.seo_description: A white-label website rescue service for agencies: white screens, broken checkouts and plugin conflicts found, fixed on staging and written up. Read more.
services.intro: Our website rescue service gets broken client sites working again without guesswork: white screens, failed checkouts, plugin conflicts and layouts wrecked by an update. Senior developers find the cause before changing anything, then fix it on staging and write it up in your brand.
services.content_html:
A website rescue service steps in when a client site is down, half-broken or too fragile for anyone to touch. You keep talking to the client while we find the cause and fix it, and you get a write-up to send under your name.

Our founder leads the work. He has nine years of PHP, WordPress, WooCommerce and Elementor work for agencies in the UK and Bangladesh. Most recently he led the WordPress team at a UK agency, so failed updates and broken checkouts are familiar ground.

What usually breaks, and where we look first

Most faults have a short list of likely causes, and we check those before changing anything. A fix without a known cause tends to come back the following week.

SymptomCauses we check first
White screen or "There has been a critical error"A PHP fatal error after a plugin, theme or PHP version update, a memory limit, or a failed auto-update
Payment taken but the order stays pendingBlocked payment gateway webhooks, WP-Cron not running, or cart and checkout pages being cached
Forms look fine but nothing arrivesMissing SMTP setup, expired spam-protection keys, or a CRM endpoint that changed
Layout broken after an updateElementor or theme version mismatch, stale generated CSS, or a minification conflict
Admin slow or locked outSecurity plugin rules, heavy background requests, or a bloated options table

We read the PHP error log, the WordPress debug log and the browser console, and ask what changed recently. On Shopify and Webflow the usual suspects are app conflicts, edited theme code and broken custom embeds.

How our website rescue service handles an outage

When a site is down or losing orders, we restore service first and fix the cause properly second. Flag the brief as urgent and we will confirm whether we can take it, and the cost, before any work starts.

We take a fresh backup before touching anything, even of a broken site. A live outage sometimes needs one small change in production, such as rolling back a plugin. We record exactly what changed, then build the lasting fix on staging with before-and-after evidence.

The Dhaka timezone (UTC+6) helps with overnight problems. Brief us at 5pm London and the fix can be ready for review at 9am.

Access goes through a shared password vault with the lowest role that does the job, and we revoke it at handover. Our security page covers the detail. If the site shows signs of a hack, such as spam redirects or unknown admin users, we switch to our malware cleanup process instead.

After the rescue: keep it fixed

Many breakages trace back to updates applied straight to the live site. Once the site is stable, a white-label maintenance plan with staged updates and nightly backups catches the next fault on staging.

Heat Pumps 4 Pools shows that pattern: our founder built the WooCommerce store, then stayed on for maintenance engineering after launch. You can open the Heat Pumps 4 Pools case study and click through the live store.

A rescue is quoted outside the monthly plans, with a written scope and fixed price before work starts. The rates page explains how plans and one-off scopes fit together. Rescue sits within our wider white-label web development service, and it suits web design agencies that inherit sites from other developers.

Questions agencies ask about website rescue

Can you fix a site another developer built?

Yes. A rescue usually means a site someone else built, often by a developer who has since left. We read the code and the change history before touching anything.

The write-up describes the cause without blaming anyone, so it stays safe to forward to your client, even if the previous developer was your own team.

How fast can you start on a site that is down?

Say it is urgent in the brief. We will tell you whether we can take it and what it costs before any work starts. If we cannot meet your timing, we say so rather than miss it.

Our UTC+6 hours mean a fault reported at the end of the UK day can be worked on overnight.

Do you rescue Shopify and Webflow sites too?

Yes. Alongside WordPress and WooCommerce, we fix Shopify themes, app conflicts and Liquid errors, and Webflow sites with broken interactions or custom code.

The method is the same on every platform: back up what exists, find the cause, fix it on a copy where the platform allows, then check the flows around it.

What if the same problem comes back?

If the fix was in the agreed scope and it breaks again, we fix it at our cost, with no invoice. If a different cause produces the same symptom, we tell you what is new and quote it before doing the work. The root-cause notes from the first rescue usually make the second diagnosis much faster.

Will you tell our client what went wrong?

No. We never contact your client. You get a plain-English write-up in your brand covering what broke, why, what we changed and how to stop it happening again.

You decide how much to share and how to frame it. If the client's in-house team needs a technical version, we can write both.

What is white-label digital marketing?

White-label digital marketing is SEO, paid media, conversion and tracking work that a partner delivers for your agency's clients under your agency's name. The partner runs the campaigns and the fixes. Your agency sells the service, owns the client relationship and sends the reports, which carry only your brand.

It works best when the channels come from one team. The landing page, the tracking and the campaign then share one owner, and a broken conversion tag never sits between two suppliers blaming each other.

What a white-label marketing agency handles for you

We run the day-to-day execution across organic search, Google Ads, Meta Ads, landing pages and tracking. You set the strategy, approve budgets and keep every client conversation.

Organic search

Keyword research mapped to pages, on-page work, content briefs, technical fixes and outreach-led link building. Our co-founder, Md Mazidul Hossain Likhon, leads SEO, with 4+ years across 50+ clients in semantic SEO, link building, GEO and AEO.

Our developers build the pages your campaigns land on, in WordPress or Next.js, and fix the forms, checkouts and booking flows that lose leads. Because the same team builds and measures, an A/B test reaches the live site instead of waiting in a developer queue.

Tracking that holds up

We implement GA4, Google Tag Manager, Consent Mode v2 and server-side events for Google Ads and Meta, and we test every conversion end to end. When the CRM and the ad platform disagree on lead numbers, there is a documented answer.

Edge cases we plan for

Some clients have their own marketer who edits campaigns too. We agree with you who changes what, and the change log records every edit we make.

Google Ads, Meta and GA4 often report different conversion counts for the same period. We write down which source each report figure comes from, so nobody compares unlike numbers in a client meeting.

You stay in charge of the strategy, budget approvals, pricing and every call with the client.

Which channel fits which client

You send the brief, we return a written scope and fixed price within two business days, and a named producer runs the work from a shared Slack Connect or WhatsApp channel. Nothing starts until you approve the scope.

Each channel gets a monthly plan. Development, SEO and paid work run in parallel, with a weekly status you can forward. Landing pages go up on a password-protected staging URL under your brand before they go live.

The team works from Dhaka (UTC+6, no daylight saving), between 09:00 and 23:00 local time. The Dhaka afternoon overlaps the UK working day, the evening overlaps US East Coast mornings and the morning overlaps the Sydney afternoon.

Builds you can open

The content structure lets the client's team maintain pages without breaking templates. That matters for campaigns, because landing pages change often and should not need a developer each time.

In-house team, freelancers or a white-label partner

A partner suits agencies whose marketing work changes month to month or spans several channels. An in-house team suits agencies with steady demand in one channel and the time to manage specialists.

The Dhaka afternoon runs alongside your working day, and a brief sent at 5pm London is in review by 9am. Consent Mode v2 matters for UK and EU traffic, so we set it up before campaigns scale, and client data sits under UK GDPR terms with the IDTA or UK Addendum.

The Dhaka evening overlaps US East Coast and Toronto mornings, and the Dhaka morning overlaps the Sydney afternoon. Work moves forward overnight on your clock, with a summary waiting in your channel when you start. Reports follow your client's spelling, currency and date format.

Questions agencies ask about white-label digital marketing

Do you guarantee leads or ROAS?

No. Results depend on the client's offer, prices, budget, competitors and how fast they follow up a lead, and much of that sits outside any agency's control.

What we commit to is the work in the scope, done properly and logged, with a monthly report that shows what changed, why, and what happens next. A partner who guarantees ROAS is guessing.

What is white-label PPC management?

The campaigns sit in accounts the client or your agency owns, the partner works through access you grant, and the reports carry your brand. Your client only ever deals with you.

Your client, or your agency if that is how you set up your clients. We never create ad accounts for your clients in our own name.

Google Ads accounts link to your manager account, and Meta assets are shared with your business portfolio as a partner. At handover, our access is removed and we confirm it in writing.

Can we brief one channel only?

Yes. Each service can be briefed on its own, whether that is Google Ads for one client or tracking fixes across five. Starting with one channel is a sensible way to test the working relationship before you add more.

Every brief gets a written scope and a fixed price within two business days, and nothing starts until you approve it.

What do the monthly reports look like?

Each report carries your agency's logo and colours and follows your template, or we build a Looker Studio dashboard to match it. Do you mark up ad spend?

The simplest set-up has the client pay Google and Meta directly on their own payment method, which keeps the spend visible to them. We quote our own work only, and what you charge your client for management is your business.

Landing pages, tracking and technical fixes come from the development side, led by our founder, Md Alamgir Hossen, a senior WordPress and Next.js developer. Never. We do not email, call or message your client, connect with them on LinkedIn, or use their work in our portfolio without your written permission.

If a client meeting needs technical detail, we brief you beforehand so you can lead it. The commitment holds during the project and after it ends.

White-label Next.js development means an outside team builds a Next.js website or web app that your agency delivers as its own work. Questions agencies ask about white-label WooCommerce development

Can you fix a checkout that keeps losing orders?

Yes. We copy the store to staging, read the gateway and server logs, and reproduce the failure before changing anything.

You get a written cause, the fix with before-and-after evidence, and a check of the checkout paths around it. If orders are failing right now, say so in the brief and we treat it as an emergency.

Which payment gateways do you set up?

Stripe, PayPal, Klarna and others the client's market needs. We configure each one and test it end to end in sandbox mode before launch, including refunds and failed payments. Merchant accounts stay in the client's name, so payouts and disputes never depend on us.

Can you move a store from Shopify or Magento to WooCommerce?

Yes. A store migration covers products, variations, customers and order history where the old platform allows export, plus a redirect for every product and category URL.

We rehearse the move on staging first, then agree a cutover window with you so the client keeps taking orders during the switch.

Will the store stay fast with a large catalogue?

Speed comes from decisions made during the build: caching that excludes the cart and checkout, an image pipeline, lean templates and a clean database. We cannot promise a score on hosting we do not control. Every store does get a performance pass before handover, with Core Web Vitals measured on real devices.

Do you build subscriptions, bookings and product configurators?

Yes, where the brief needs them. We use established WooCommerce extensions when they fit.

When the client's rules go further, such as pricing that depends on several product options, we write custom code. The scope states which approach we are taking and why, so you can explain it to your client.

services.heading: White-label WordPress plugin development

services.intro: Our white-label WordPress plugin development turns a client requirement into one plugin with one job, delivered under your brand. Each plugin has its own admin screens, settings and update path, written to WordPress coding standards so the next developer can read it.
services.content_html:
What white-label WordPress plugin development means for your agency

White-label WordPress plugin development means an outside team writes a custom plugin that your agency delivers as its own. The plugin header, text domain, PHP namespace and documentation all carry your agency's name, and your client never hears from us.

We build and publish plugins of our own too. The SoftVolt AI Voice Agent plugin is free on WordPress.org. We follow the same plugin guidelines on our own code as on yours.

When a custom plugin is the right call

Build a custom plugin when the requirement is specific to the client's business, or when the existing options carry more risk than they save. Typical briefs:

  • The only plugin that does the job is abandoned, bloated or licensed per site across dozens of client installs.
  • Pricing, eligibility, booking or approval rules that no settings screen can express.
  • An integration with the client's CRM, ERP or booking system through its API.
  • Five plugins stacked to reach one outcome, each with its own updates and conflicts.
  • WooCommerce cart, checkout or order logic that needs hooks and filters.

When a well-maintained plugin already does the job, we say so in the scope. A custom plugin is something your client keeps for years, so it has to earn its place.

How we build plugins the next developer can maintain

Every plugin follows WordPress coding standards and the security basics that most plugin problems come from skipping:

  • Namespaced PHP and prefixed options, hooks and database tables, so nothing clashes with other plugins.
  • Capability checks and nonces on every admin action, sanitised input and escaped output.
  • Settings built on the WordPress Settings API, and REST endpoints with permission callbacks.
  • Versioned database migrations that run on update, and an uninstall routine that removes what the plugin created.
  • Translation-ready strings, plus WP-CLI commands where the client's team runs bulk tasks.
  • A readme, inline documentation and a handover note in your brand.

For store logic, see our WooCommerce development service. Plugin work also sits within our wider white-label WordPress development service.

Pricing and ownership

A plugin gets a written scope and a fixed price before we write any code. The price moves with the number of admin screens, integrations and data migrations, and with the update path you need. Anything outside your monthly plan is quoted separately, and the plans are listed on our rates page.

We transfer the repository at handover, so your agency or your client owns the code. Access to the client's site follows our security and confidentiality practices, from a shared vault to access removed at handover.

Questions agencies ask about white-label WordPress plugin development

Who owns the plugin code?

You do, or your client, whichever you agree between you. We transfer the Git repository at handover, and the plugin header, namespace and documentation carry your agency's name.

We never show the plugin in a portfolio or anywhere public without your written permission, and we never contact your client about it.

Can you publish the plugin on WordPress.org under our name?

Yes, if you want it public. We prepare the readme, the assets and the code to the WordPress.org plugin guidelines.

You submit it from your own account, so the listing is yours. We have been through the same process with our own free plugin. Many client plugins stay private and update from your repository instead.

How do updates reach client sites?

The update path is written into the scope. Options include WordPress.org, a private repository with an update checker, or manual releases with a changelog.

Each release runs its own database migrations, so a site that skips a version still upgrades in order. We test every release on staging before it reaches the live site.

Will a custom plugin conflict with other plugins?

Prefixed code and namespaces avoid most clashes, and we test against the client's active theme and plugins on a staging copy. Nobody can rule out every future conflict, because other plugins keep changing. If a defect in the agreed scope appears after launch, we fix it at our cost.

Can you fix or extend a plugin someone else wrote?

Yes. We start with a short audit covering code quality, security issues, licence terms and how much of the plugin the client actually uses.

You then get a written recommendation to extend, fork or replace it, with a fixed price for each option. You choose before quoting your client.

services.heading: WordPress malware removal and security

services.intro: Our WordPress malware removal service cleans hacked client sites for agencies, under your brand. We find the infection and the way in, close it, rotate the credentials and hand the site back with monitoring in place.
services.content_html:
A hacked client site is an agency problem first, because the client calls you, not the host. Our WordPress malware removal service gives you a senior developer who triages the site and does the cleanup. You keep the client conversation, and we write the recovery plan you forward.

What our WordPress malware removal service covers

It covers the whole incident, from the first look at the site to the hardening that follows. Removing the visible malware is only one step.

We work from a fresh copy of the site. We check core files against the official WordPress checksums with WP-CLI, and search the database as well as the files.

Then we patch the way in, whether that was an outdated plugin, a nulled theme or a weak hosting setting. We rotate every credential, cut admin roles back to least privilege and turn on two-factor login. Every step goes into a written log your client update can draw on.

The first hours after a hack

Preserve the evidence, check how far the infection has spread, then clean. Restoring an old backup straight over a hacked site can bring the same backdoor back.

  1. Take a full copy of files, database and server logs before anyone changes anything.
  2. Check every other site on the same hosting account, because infections spread between sites that share a server user.
  3. Stop the harm to visitors: block the redirect, or put the site behind a holding page.
  4. Change the hosting, SFTP and database passwords, then change them again once the cleanup is finished.
  5. Give the client a short, factual update, using the facts in our written recovery plan.

Why cleaned sites get reinfected

A site gets reinfected when the cleanup removes what is visible and leaves the door open. These are the places we check on every job:

  • Hidden administrator accounts, including ones with ordinary-looking names
  • PHP files in the uploads folder, where no PHP should run
  • Must-use plugins and scheduled tasks that rewrite files after a cleanup
  • Code injected into the database, in options, widgets and post content
  • Nulled premium plugins and themes, which often arrive with a backdoor built in
  • Stolen hosting or SFTP passwords, which make every other fix pointless

If the entry point was an abandoned plugin with no fix, we replace it. Where nothing suitable exists, our WordPress plugin development team can build a lean replacement.

Pricing and what happens after the cleanup

Each cleanup gets a written recovery plan and a fixed price before work starts. Mark the brief as urgent: if we can hit your deadline we will say what it costs, and if we cannot, we will say that instead.

Plans and pricing are on our rates page. Blocklist removal requests and the Google review request are part of the job. The blocklist owners set their own timing, so we never promise a date.

Once the site is clean, a white-label maintenance plan keeps it patched, scanned and backed up. If the hack broke features as well, website rescue and bug fixing picks those up.

Questions agencies ask about WordPress malware removal

How fast can you start on a hacked site?

Send the brief marked urgent, with hosting access shared through a password vault. Triage and a written recovery plan follow within hours, and the plan names the fixed price before cleanup starts. Our team works from Dhaka (UTC+6), so a site that breaks late in your day can be worked on while you sleep.

Can you get the site off Google's warning list?

We do everything on our side: clean the site, remove the cause, then request a review in Search Console and ask other blocklists to delist it. Google and the blocklist owners decide when the warning comes off, so we never promise a date. The written log gives your client a full record of what was fixed.

How do you handle client data during a cleanup?

Carefully, and in writing. Credentials come through a shared vault, never email, and we take the least access the job needs. For UK and EU personal data we work under a data processing agreement with the IDTA or SCCs.

We revoke our access at handover and confirm it in writing. Our security page lists every practice.

The host has suspended the account. Can you still help?

Yes, as long as the host allows file or SSH access during the suspension. We clean every site on the account, document what we removed and send the host the evidence it asks for. If the host will not reopen the account, we can move the clean site as a separate website migration.

How do we stop it happening again?

Nobody can promise a site will never be hacked, but many reinfections come from the same few gaps. We close them at handover with patched plugins, fresh credentials, least-privilege roles and two-factor login. After that, a maintenance plan keeps updates, malware scanning and backups running each month, with a report in your brand.

services.seo_description: Workflow automation for agencies: n8n, Make or custom code that connects CRMs, forms and ad platforms, with retries and alerts. Get a fixed-price scope.
services.intro: We build workflow automation for agencies and their clients in n8n, Make or custom code, under your brand. Leads, CRM records and report data move on their own, and a failed run raises an alert instead of losing a lead.
services.content_html:
Workflow automation for agencies connects the tools a client already pays for, so data moves without anyone copying it by hand. We build it under your brand, document it for your account team and hand it over with every account in your name or your client's.

What workflow automation for agencies covers

It covers any process where a person moves data between two systems. If someone re-keys it, checks it every Friday or forwards it between inboxes, it can usually be automated.

Typical briefs look like this:

  • Website form and Meta lead form entries pushed into HubSpot or Pipedrive within minutes, deduplicated and assigned to an owner
  • A signed proposal that creates the project, the shared folder and a draft invoice
  • Monthly report data gathered into Google Sheets before the account manager opens it
  • WooCommerce orders passed to the client's accounting or fulfilment tools
  • Your own agency's onboarding and renewal steps, as well as your clients' processes

Most of these need no AI at all. When a step involves reading free text, such as sorting enquiries by intent, it becomes part of our white-label AI automation service.

n8n, Make or custom code: how we choose

We pick the tool the client's team can live with after handover, then check it against volume and data rules. The scope names the choice and the reason.

OptionFits whenWatch out for
n8n (cloud or self-hosted)Many steps, branching logic, or data that should stay on infrastructure you controlSelf-hosting means someone patches, monitors and backs up the server
MakeThe client's team wants to edit flows visually and volumes are moderateUsage-based pricing rises with volume, so we model it at scoping
Custom Node.js codeHigh volumes, strict validation, or logic too complex for visual nodesChanges need a developer, so it suits stable processes

If the client already runs flows in another tool, tell us in the brief. Sometimes the right call is to fix what exists rather than rebuild it.

What makes a workflow safe to rely on

Error handling makes it safe. A workflow that fails quietly is worse than none, because everyone assumes the leads are still arriving.

Every workflow we hand over includes:

  • Retries with a delay for temporary errors, such as a rate limit or a CRM timeout
  • An alert to a named person when a run fails for good, with the record attached
  • Duplicate protection, so a webhook sent twice creates one CRM contact, not two
  • Checks on phone numbers, emails and required fields before anything is written
  • A run log your team can search when a client asks where a lead went

Credentials for each connected tool sit in a shared vault, with the least access the workflow needs. Our security page explains how we handle them and how access ends at handover.

Pricing and where it fits

A one-off workflow gets a written scope and a fixed price within two business days of the brief. The number of systems, the state of their data and the error handling the process needs set that price.

Ongoing automation work fits our Premium plan, which includes AI automation, or Enterprise, which covers the full white-label suite. Tool subscriptions such as n8n cloud or Make are billed at cost or held in your accounts. Compare the plans on our rates page.

If the client's leads come from a WordPress site, our free SoftVolt AI Voice Agent plugin sends each lead to an n8n webhook. It ships with a ready-made workflow that passes leads on to Google Sheets, a CRM or WhatsApp.

Questions agencies ask about workflow automation

Can you work inside the client's existing n8n or Make account?

Yes, and we prefer it, because the client keeps ownership of the workflows and the billing. We ask for a user with only the access the work needs, shared through a password vault rather than email. At handover we remove our access, confirm it in writing and leave a runbook so your team can support each workflow.

Does workflow automation need AI?

Usually not. Moving, checking and deduplicating data is a rules job, and plain logic does it more cheaply and the same way every time.

We add an AI step only where a workflow has to read free text, such as an enquiry or an email reply. A person then approves anything the AI writes before it reaches a customer.

What happens when a connected tool changes its API?

The workflow alerts a named person instead of failing in silence, and the runbook lists what to check first. Upstream changes are covered by your monthly plan or quoted as a small fixed-price change. Defects in our own work, inside the agreed scope, are fixed at our cost.

Can you automate our agency's own processes?

Yes. Your onboarding, reporting and renewal steps are workflows like any other. For example, a renewal alert can reach the account manager well before a client contract ends, with the latest figures attached.

The same rules apply: a written scope, a fixed price, and accounts that stay in your name.

Can a workflow send CRM outcomes back to Google Ads or Meta?

Yes. A workflow can send qualified or closed leads from the CRM back to the ad platforms, so bidding learns from real outcomes.

It depends on consent and on capturing click identifiers when the form is submitted. We scope it alongside our analytics and conversion tracking work.
